response: No, low-tone sudden deafness does not inevitably progress to Meniere's disease. While some patients with low-tone sudden deafness may develop Meniere's disease, many others do not. The prognosis varies depending on individual factors, and some people may experience spontaneous recovery or stabilization of their hearing loss. Regular monitoring and follow-up with an audiologist or ear, nose, and throat (ENT) specialist can help track any changes in hearing and provide appropriate management.
